claims.text: The baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa, compressive strength of 1314 MPa, and fracture strain of 13.5%.
The intervention is approximately 10 at.% W substituted for Ta in HfZrTiTa0.53.
HfZrTiTa0.53W0.1 represents the proposed approximately 10 at.% W substitution.
Controlled thermomechanical processing of the W-modified alloy will encourage fine W-rich precipitate formation.
W addition will promote a refined dual-phase microstructure in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Fine W-rich precipitates will pin dislocations and impede their motion.
Dynamic precipitation and grain refinement will provide additional dislocation barriers and enhance dynamic work hardening.
The W-induced microstructure will delay dynamic recrystallization.
Enhanced strain hardening will delay local thermal softening and the onset of adiabatic shear bands.
The W-modified alloy will have higher dynamic yield and compressive strengths than the baseline alloy.
The W-modified alloy will have a higher fracture strain and improved uniform deformability.
The W-modified alloy will resist shear localization and form adiabatic shear bands later than the baseline alloy.
The W-modified alloy will absorb more impact-induced energy before failure.
The prediction applies to adiabatic dynamic compression at strain rates from approximately 1300 to 2100 s^-1.
A reported W10 HEA exhibits increased dynamic yield strength and high-rate ductility, including fracture strains of 20% and 24% at 2000 and 3000 s^-1.
In dual-phase AlCrFe2Ni2, adiabatic shear bands appear during dynamic deformation through dynamic recrystallization associated with competition between strain-rate hardening and thermal softening.
The effectiveness of the intervention at lower strain rates or under tensile loading is untested.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as approximately 10 at.% W substituted for Ta, but the stated formula HfZrTiTa0.53W0.1 retains the full Ta coefficient and contains only about 2.75 at.% W after normalization; it is an addition rather than a 10 at.% substitution.

The predicted outcomes are phrased relative to a quasi-static baseline, whereas the falsification experiment compares dynamically tested baseline and modified samples. These are different reference comparisons, so the benchmark for improvement is not consistently defined.
